name: Intro Format Gate
use_when: The edit needs to decide whether a formal intro bumper should exist at all.
A podcast, show, course, creator page, or repeatable social series needs brand packaging.
The intro can build trust, authority, or series identity faster than immediate content alone.
avoid_when: A normal 8-12 minute YouTube tutorial or essay should start delivering the title promise immediately.
The intro delays a feed-first short that already needs a hook inside the first seconds.
The bumper is only a legacy habit, logo vanity, or old channel template.
The audience is there for a specific answer and does not need brand context first.

timeline_pattern.podcast_rule: Long podcasts or shows can justify a short brand/proof/outcome intro because the viewer expects a program identity.
timeline_pattern.series_rule: Repeatable Instagram/Reels/social series can use very short intros to identify the series and promise.
timeline_pattern.midlength_youtube_rule: For ordinary mid-length YouTube videos, skip formal intros unless the brand proof materially increases trust.
timeline_pattern.duration_rule: Use about 10-15 seconds maximum for long-form/show intros and about 3-5 seconds for social series intros.

motion.rule: Use motion only if it communicates brand, authority, or outcome faster than static text.

sound.rule: Intro music should signal premium identity quickly, then hand off cleanly to the main voice or content.

captions.rule: Do not duplicate intro bumper text with ordinary captions unless accessibility requires it.

color.rule: Intro color should match the show or creator identity without making the first value cue harder to read.

implementation.ffmpeg: Represent the intro decision as metadata: introAllowed, format, maxDuration, introPurpose, and bodyStartTime. Concatenate a pre-rendered bumper only when the gate passes.
implementation.remotion: Create an IntroGate object with format, maxDurationFrames, purpose, brandRequired, proofRequired, and skipReason fields.
implementation.blender: Render a branded bumper only for show/series formats where a reusable opener is justified.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Use a short saved intro template only for podcast/show/social-series packaging; delete it from ordinary answer-first videos.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Nest the bumper and place markers for intro_start, intro_end, and body_start; keep the nest disabled when the intro gate fails.

common_mistakes: Adding a formal intro to every YouTube video because it feels professional.
Using a long logo bumper before the viewer knows the value.
Treating a social-series intro like a long YouTube intro.
Letting a reusable template age into an outdated channel habit.
qc: Can the editor name why this format needs an intro bumper?
Would the target viewer prefer immediate content over this intro?
Is the intro within the correct duration cap for the platform?
Does the body start before the viewer feels delayed?
If the intro is removed, does the edit become clearer or weaker?
